home.title: IIPHA
home.lead: Our vision is to cultivate a cohesive community that offers distinct opportunities to contribute to humanitarian and professional assistance, particularly in the aftermath of disasters concerning Iran. Our mission is to monitor, regulate, supervise and pertain to healthcare standards and leverage action plans for our objectives.

blocks.label: Outreach to Iran
blocks.body: IIPHA aims to create a platform that unites and empowers the Iranian diaspora civil society by engaging with the media and obtaining an influential voice in the centres of power and international organizations, global affairs, key decision-makers, governmental authorities, officials, and society at large worldwide. We focus on medical issues related to justice and human rights in Iran.

blocks.label: We provide care
blocks.body: IIPHA is a non-profit, US-based, non-partisan, and gender-neutral association weathering the worldwide civil social demands on behalf of all its stakeholders and members. It is a civil action and advocacy association composed of healthcare professionals of Iranian heritage.

home.statementTitle: IIPHA and other social activist groups stand in solidarity with Iranian nurses
statement: Like other parts of Iranian society, nurses have been struggling with numerous social, economic, and professional challenges in recent years. However, none of these overwhelming hardships have prevented nurses from their primary mission.

Every fellow citizen vividly remembers that during the peak of COVID-19, while the government’s unscientific policies and adherence to superstitious and ideological approaches were exponentially increasing the death rates, it was these devoted healthcare workers who, by sacrificing their own lives and health, strived to reduce the mortality rate of our compatriots.

Following the recent events in Iran and the protests after the murder of Mahsa Zhina Amini, the United Nations has established an Independent International Fact-Finding Mission (FFMI) to investigate the deteriorating situation of human rights in the Islamic Republic of Iran. The FFMI has invited those whom the Islamic Republic has harmed to send evidence of human rights violations to this group.
home.casesLabel: We are dedicated to our mission
casesIntro: This is the time that we, physicians and health workers in the diaspora, need to rise up to pay back what we owe to our mother nation — especially in these turbulent times when our nation needs support more than ever.

There are a number of physicians close to the regime who have sadly forsaken the oath they took when becoming a doctor. We take these matters very seriously and are in the process of gathering evidence, verification and building legal cases against them. The cases include but are not limited to:
cases: Spreading misinformation and pseudoscience regarding diseases and means of protection — especially COVID-19 and its vaccines — to their benefit, endangering the lives of millions in Iran
Denying safe sex protection to the population on the order of the Supreme Leader, which denies protection against sexually transmitted disease
Breach of confidentiality of their patients, and handing over injured protesters to the authorities
Using their status to doctor statistics and clinical data
Reporting fellow physicians who have been treating injured protesters
home.casesNote: If you have any information or evidence, please send it to us at
home.whistleBody: Whether it concerns arrested health workers, victims of the security forces, abuse of ambulances, misleading death certificates, or any related issue, you can inform us anonymously and securely.
home.whistleQuestion: Do you have critical information that can help us shine a light on the atrocities and the breach of health-related human rights in Iran?

about.title: About — IIPHA
about.claim: IIPHA strives to provide a platform to unite and empower the Iranian diaspora civil society
about.lead: A non-profit, US-based, non-partisan, gender-neutral association composed of healthcare professionals of Iranian heritage — registered in California under section 501(c)(3), EIN 92-1415767.
intro: IIPHA is a civil action and advocacy association that aims to address Iranians’ social determinants of health on behalf of all its stakeholders and members. This particularly includes tackling systems that shape the conditions of daily life for people, including “economic policies and systems, development agendas, social norms, social policies and political systems.” [1]

IIPHA strives to provide a platform to unite and empower the Iranian diaspora civil society in order to collectively address issues pertaining to justice and human rights with a focus on Iranians’ health and well-being, whether residing inside Iran or out. To do so, IIPHA follows a social medicine model [2] by trying to understand Iranians’ health experiences, needs, and expectations, participating in the relevant decision-making processes, and designing and delivering proper interventions aimed at improving their health conditions. As such, IIPHA’s healthcare professionals engage with the health issues of Iranians on three overlapping levels:

levels.label: Individual
levels.body: addressing direct health needs of patients

levels.label: Community
levels.body: collaborating with various communities, particularly the most disadvantaged groups

levels.label: Society
levels.body: informing policymaking processes and collaborating with the relevant international organizations

about.outcomes: The outcomes of IIPHA’s endeavors will be used to raise awareness and advocate for the improvement of Iranians’ social determinants of health by obtaining an influential voice in the centers of power and international organizations, global affairs, key decision-makers, governmental authorities, and officials, as well as society at large. Moreover, our findings could assist legal investigations on potential human rights violations by the Islamic Republic of Iran, namely the United Nations’ Independent International Fact-Finding Mission on the Islamic Republic of Iran. [3]

mission.title: Our mission — IIPHA
mission.lead: IIPHA is a US-registered nonprofit, nonpartisan, and gender-inclusive organization that works on behalf of its members and supporters to advance universal civil and humanitarian causes. It is an association of healthcare professionals of Iranian heritage engaged in advocacy and civic action.
body: IIPHA strives to create a platform that promotes solidarity and empowers the Iranian community abroad. We pursue this goal by engaging with and influencing the media, developing a strong and effective voice within centers of power, international institutions and networks, and reaching policymakers, government officials, and the international community on issues related to justice, human rights, and healthcare.

Our aim is to build a cohesive network capable of creating unique opportunities for humanitarian and medical assistance, particularly in response to recent crises in Iran. Our mission includes monitoring health and healthcare standards, maintaining meaningful engagement in these areas, and developing practical plans to achieve our objectives.
mission.chapters: The association will establish affiliated chapters in other countries. Each chapter or affiliated group will be named according to the country in which it operates — for example, IIPHA Canada, IIPHA UK, IIPHA USA, and so forth. Each chapter will have the authority to make independent decisions regarding its internal affairs.
mission.bylaws: For more information, please refer to IIPHA’s bylaws.

join.title: Join us — IIPHA
join.lead: IIPHA is composed of hard-working volunteers who have another day job, and a family to support — just like you. But we cannot operate without your help. There are many ways you can help us, such as spreading the word. Specifically, you can support us in these three ways:

ways.label: Become a member
ways.body: Members are an essential part of any not-for-profit organization. By paying an annual membership fee and taking part in IIPHA’s general assemblies, you enable us to cover our expenses and help shape the direction of IIPHA. Based on your interests and skills, you can also contribute to the work itself — welcome, though not expected. A member needs to be a physician, dentist, nurse, pharmacist, or any other profession in the healthcare providers family.

ways.label: Become a volunteer
ways.body: If you have the skills we need and the time to contribute to the work of IIPHA, you can become a volunteer without becoming a member or paying an annual fee — although one-off or regular donations are highly appreciated. After your application, we will review it and get back to you based on our priorities and needs.

ways.label: Become an advocate
ways.body: If you do not have the time to contribute and do not qualify for membership, you can still help us by registering to receive our free newsletter — and by sharing what we publish.

details.label: Members
details.body: Join the IIPHA community and make a difference. As a member, you will have the opportunity to be actively involved in the life of our organization and participate in our general assemblies, where you can share your ideas and make your voice heard. Your membership fees and donations are essential for us as a non-profit organization to continue our work and cover our expenses. Our task forces are led by dedicated volunteers, just like you, who are passionate about making a positive impact in Iran.

details.label: Volunteers
details.body: A large number of Iranians inside and outside the country have been looking for a way to help their fellow citizens. If you are one of these people, IIPHA invites you to use your skills to help protect the lives, safety and health of Iranian citizens. Alternatively, by providing us your email, you register as an advocate and will receive our free newsletter.

donate.title: Donate — IIPHA
donate.lead: As a not-for-profit organization, we are completely dependent on donations and contributions from the public, as well as membership fees, to cover our expenses — which are mainly the charges for the specialist human rights lawyers working with us.
donate.banner: If you are a healthcare provider outside Iran, the best way to help is to become a member.
donate.note: You may contribute to our funds using PayPal by clicking the button above and following the instructions when the new page opens.
donate.bannerBody: Otherwise, in addition to becoming a volunteer, you can help us by donating as little as $10.
